summary: @ornikar/jest-config-react-native-web preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes opaque bundled payload
details: The package advertises itself as an @ornikar jest preset but ships no jest configuration: the declared main jest-preset.js contains only `throw new Error('Use @ornikar/jest-config-react-native/web instead');`. All behavior is in an obfuscated preinstall script (setup.mjs, identifiers renamed to `_0xNNNN` with lookup-object control flow) that downloads the Bun runtime archive from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<arch>.zip`, extracts it via a hand-rolled ZIP reader, chmods it executable (mode 493), and invokes it via execFileSync against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) using a large numeric+string constant array, a rotating dispatch function, single-letter globals, and an alphabet-based string decoder — unreadable by Node and unreviewable statically. The package's stated purpose (a jest preset) has no need for Bun or a 727KB compiled bundle. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: installing the package on default `npm install` pulls a runtime solely to execute an opaque payload under it, bypassing Node-based scanners. The @ornikar scope name impersonates the legitimate Ornikar configuration packages.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
